recentChanges.text: Cook Political Report moved four governor races toward Democrats: Alaska to Lean D (reports say from Toss Up) and shifts in Nebraska, Vermont and Oklahoma (new categories not stated in sources read).
Sabato's Crystal Ball moved the Minnesota Senate race from Likely Democratic to Leans Democratic ('Minnesota Senate to Leans Democratic'); 270toWin logs the Crystal Ball update as Oct 14.

Cook House ratings update: MT-01 Lean R to Toss Up; FL-25 Toss Up to Lean D; OH-01 Lean D to Likely D; MN-01, NY-21, OH-10, OH-15 and SC-01 Likely R to Lean R; FL-16, KS-02 and NE-01 into Likely R (derived by comparing Cook's Oct 9 and Oct 16 lists; counts now 185/17/12/21/13/16/171).

Cook Political Report Senate changes: Minnesota Likely D to Lean D; South Carolina Likely R to Lean R; Mississippi Solid R to Likely R (Jessica Taylor cited candidate quality; Cook said its overall Senate outlook is unchanged).
Inside Elections moved the Texas Senate race from Tilt R to Toss-up (270toWin change log, Oct 23).
Fox News polls released Oct 22-23 show Maine (Jackson 49, Collins 49) and Texas (Talarico 49, Paxton 49) tied and Brown +5 in Ohio; NYT/Siena (Oct 21) has the generic ballot at D 52, R 41.

Governors: Cook moved Florida and Texas from Likely to Lean R; Inside Elections moved Alaska (Lean R) and Ohio (Tilt R) to Toss-up and Oklahoma Safe to Likely R. Oct 6: Sabato moved Alaska Toss-up to Leans D and Oregon Likely to Leans D (context; before Oct 11).

Sabato's Crystal Ball governor changes (Kyle Kondik, 'The Governors: Ohio to Leans Democratic Among Other Changes'): Ohio Toss-up to Leans Democratic; Michigan Leans Democratic to Likely Democratic; Alabama and Oklahoma Safe Republican to Likely Republican. The Ohio and Michigan Senate ratings were left unchanged. (The desk's file had carried Ohio as Leans R; the article states the prior rating as Toss-up.)
Cook Political Report moved the Ohio governor's race from Toss Up to Lean Democrat (Jessica Taylor, 'Amid Ad Uproar, Ohio Governor's Race Moves From Toss Up to Lean Democrat').

Cook Political Report House update (Erin Covey): 19 more races moved toward Democrats, including six Toss Up to Lean D (four with Republican incumbents) and two open seats Lean R to Toss Up; Cook now rates 220 seats Solid/Likely/Lean D, 198 Solid/Likely/Lean R and 17 Toss Up, and says the likeliest outcome is a Democratic gain of 12 to 22 seats. District-level list is subscriber-only and not captured.

Rasmussen Reports poll listed by RCP on Oct 24 has the Texas Senate race tied, Talarico 45, Paxton 45 (field dates and sample not shown on the listing). No Cook, Sabato or Inside Elections Senate or governor rating changes were logged Oct 24-25.

Sabato's Crystal Ball Senate changes (post 'Democrats Appear to Hold Narrow Senate Edge with Week to Go'): Florida Safe R to Likely R; South Carolina Likely R to Leans R; North Carolina Leans D to Likely D. The same post moved 16 House races toward Democrats (districts not listed in the sources read).

Sabato's Crystal Ball ('A Rating Change Appetizer'): Louisiana Senate Safe R to Likely R (Kondik cites early-vote data from John Couvillon showing strong Black turnout); Minnesota Senate Leans D to Likely D. Crystal Ball's Senate outlook: 49 D, 46 R, 5 Toss-ups; final forecast due Monday Nov. 2. Date of the post per Balloon Juice's Oct 29 map comparison; The Hill reported it Oct 30.

Cook Political Report moved 12 more House races toward Democrats: among them CO-05 (Crank) Lean R to Toss Up, PA-01 (Fitzpatrick) Lean R to Toss Up, SC-01 (open) Lean R to Toss Up, PA-08 (Bresnahan) Toss Up to Lean D, OH-09 (Kaptur) Toss Up to Lean D; 18 Toss Ups remain. Forbes: Democrats would hold 240 seats if they won every Toss Up and every seat they are favored in; Cook projects a minimum pickup of five seats.
